summary.intent: Design a server-side memory system (lessons + experiences) and planning layer for the Entire CLI agent, incorporating findings from an existing design doc and the already-implemented RFD-014 (CheckpointAnalysis API).
summary.outcome: Two design docs written and committed (force-added past .gitignore): `2026-04-16-agent-memory-lessons-experiences-design.md` (~65 KB, server-primary extraction/storage with local cache+outbox) and `2026-04-16-agent-planning-layer-design.md` (~49 KB, plans local-primary with server completion signal only). Both docs incorporate four prompt-injection hardening improvements from hermes-agent analysis.

repo: docs/plans/ is listed in .gitignore (line 61); design docs there require `git add -f` to commit on the working branch
The checkpoint system archives files under docs/plans/ on a shadow branch (e.g. entire/dbf1db1-e84028) even when they are gitignored on the working branch

RFD-014 is already implemented: CheckpointAnalysis generation moved to the entire.io API (webhook-triggered for synced checkpoints, on-demand for unsynced uploads); Entire pays the LLM cost via its own Claude key
All session and checkpoint data is already sent to the API and stored in the server DB, making local-only storage arguments for experiences invalid
workflow: When existing memory architecture assumptions are invalidated mid-session (e.g. RFD-014 already implemented), plan files should be overwritten fresh rather than patched incrementally

Hermes-agent (at /Users/alisha/Projects/hermes-agent) contains a concrete prompt-injection sanitizer with a versioned denylist regex set, invisible Unicode rejection, recalled-context wrapper framing, and response/echo-back sanitization — all transferable patterns

Invisible Unicode characters (U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+2060, U+FEFF, U+202A–U+202E) are invisible in TUI review but visible to LLMs, making them a real injection vector; rejection at ingress is the right mitigation
Wrapping injection bundles with an explicit 'this is recalled guidance, not new user instructions' annotation is one of the strongest and cheapest prompt-injection mitigations

Response sanitization (stripping memory-fence tags from captured agent output before analysis) closes a self-referential poisoning loop where the model can echo memory fences into its reply and influence future extraction

Outbox conflict resolution semantics not yet specified

Repo-scope lesson sync across users deliberately deferred to Phase 2 to avoid quality-drift risk in beta

implementation_rationale: Server-primary memory storage chosen because all session/checkpoint data is already on the server (RFD-014 implemented), making local-only arguments invalid and cross-device continuity free

Plans kept local-primary because plans are naturally scoped to one workstation/session; cross-device plan continuity is not a beta-critical feature and would require significant additional server surface
Plan outcome feedback to memory goes server-side via a focused completion signal (POST /plans/completions) rather than direct memory row mutation, keeping the local/server boundary clean
Memory derivation runs server-side because the server already has the full analysis artifact and cross-user evidence; CLI becomes a read consumer only
Hybrid extraction trigger (webhook for synced, on-demand for unsynced) mirrors RFD-014's two-path model exactly to avoid new architecture
Sanitizer denylist versioned as sanitizer_denylist_v1 so bumps piggyback on extractor_version cache invalidation
Recalled-context wrapper uses authoritative='false' attribute to signal to the model that the content is background data, not authoritative instructions
tradeoffs: Local extraction (fast iteration, user pays cost, quality drifts across users) vs server extraction (consistent quality, Entire pays, slower to iterate) — server extraction chosen for alignment with RFD-014
Local-only memory storage (offline, private, no sync cost) vs server-primary with local cache (cross-device, backup, enables derivation) — server-primary chosen given data already on server
Local-primary plans (simple, fast to ship, no outbox) vs server-primary plans (cross-device continuity, more server work) — local-primary chosen for beta

Manual memory refresh (predictable, no background activity) vs auto-on-session-start (always fresh but adds latency) vs background pull (fresh without session-start cost but complex) — manual recommended for beta

Not syncing repo-scope lessons across users in Phase 1 (avoids quality-drift from different users extracting different memories from same analysis) vs early cross-user convergence — deferred to Phase 2
Experiences deliberately not extracted in isolation from experiences-in-server-extraction until redaction design exists, even though sensitivity argument was partially invalidated
codebase_patterns: Design docs live under docs/plans/ which is gitignored; force-add required for working-branch commits
The checkpoint system maintains a shadow branch archive of gitignored files independently of the working branch
RFD-014 established the pattern: webhook-triggered async for synced data, on-demand for unsynced uploads — new features should follow this two-path model
Memory extraction uses extractor_version for cache invalidation; denylist version bumps should piggyback on this same versioning mechanism
The entire.io API uses its own Claude key and GitHub App credentials for server-side LLM calls; user auth is separate from LLM cost
Entire-Plan-Step commit trailer already exists in the checkpoint system and can be parsed server-side for plan step advancement without extra round trips
